exhibits.title: Spot Price
exhibits.statement: Solana (SOL) traded at $100.23 as of 2026-10-27 13:31:53 UTC, +0.82% over one hour and -0.65% over twenty-four hours.

exhibits.title: 24-Hour Trading Range
exhibits.statement: Over twenty-four hours the price ranged from $99.0900 to $102.48; spot sits at 34% of that range.

exhibits.title: Seven-Day Trend
exhibits.statement: Price is -3.03% over seven days. The 24-hour average ($100.40) is below the 72-hour average ($100.99). Spot is 7.68% below the seven-day high of $108.56 and 1.15% above the seven-day low of $99.0900.

exhibits.title: Volatility & Momentum
exhibits.statement: Realized volatility computed from hourly closes is 2.35% per day. The 14-hour relative strength index reads 50.4, conventionally neutral.

exhibits.title: Liquidity
exhibits.statement: Twenty-four-hour trading volume was $2.4 billion, equal to 4.05% of the $59.14 billion market capitalization.

exhibits.title: Market Sentiment
exhibits.statement: The Crypto Fear & Greed Index reads 48 ("Neutral"), versus 55 7 days earlier.

exhibits.title: Chainlink Price Feed
exhibits.statement: The Chainlink SOL/USD Data Feed on Ethereum mainnet last reported $100.51, 14 hours before the spot quote and +0.28% against the spot price in Exhibit A. Practice positions are entered and settled at this mark.

arguments.text:
May it please the Court.  

1. The spot price of SOL is firmly above the lower bound of its 24‑hour range, sitting at 34% of that range, indicating limited downside risk and a buffer against further intraday declines [Ex. B].  

2. Realized volatility is modest at 2.35% per day and the RSI is neutral at 50.4, suggesting a stable market environment conducive to a long practice position without excessive price swing risk [Ex. D].  

3. Liquidity is robust, with $2.4 billion traded in the last 24 hours, representing over 4% of market cap, and the Chainlink price feed, the settlement benchmark, is only 0.28% above the spot, confirming reliable pricing for settlement [Ex. E, G].  

The Bull rests.

May it please the Court.  

1. The spot price is modestly up +0.82 % in the last hour while sitting only 34 % up the 24‑hour range, indicating a nascent bullish thrust that is not yet priced into the Chainlink feed, which lags 14 hours and is $0.28 higher than spot [Ex. A, B, G].  

2. Realized volatility is low at 2.35 % per day, providing a stable backdrop for a short‑term paper trade, and the RSI of 50.4 confirms a neutral momentum that can be nudged lower without triggering stop‑loss cascades [Ex. D].  

3. Liquidity is ample—$2.4 billion traded in 24 hours, representing 4.05 % of market cap—so a modest short position can be entered and exited cleanly, while the Fear & Greed Index has slipped from 55 to 48, signaling waning bullish sentiment [Ex. E, F].  

The Bear rests.

Your Honor, the Bear’s first point collapses under Exhibit B: the price sits at only 34 % of the 24‑hour range, a clear sign the upward move is modest and already reflected in the Chainlink feed, which is actually $0.28 above spot, not lagging beneath it [Ex. A, B, G]. The second point rests on a “low” volatility premise, yet Exhibit D shows realized volatility of 2.35 % per day—well above the sub‑1 % levels that define a truly tranquil market, and the RSI of 50.4 is perfectly neutral, offering no impetus for a downward nudge [Ex. D]. Thus the Bear’s bullish thrust and volatility arguments are unsubstantiated. Nothing further.

Your Honor, the Bull’s first point ignores the evident weakness in the seven‑day trend: SOL is down 3.03% over the week and sits 7.68% below its recent high of $108.56, showing bearish pressure despite a modest 24‑hour position [Ex. C]. The second point rests on a “neutral” RSI, yet a neutral reading at 50.4 signals no bullish momentum and, combined with realized volatility of 2.35%—still sufficient to erode a short‑term gain—provides no safety net for a long stance [Ex. D]. Moreover, the market sentiment index has slipped to 48 from 55, indicating waning optimism that undermines the Bull’s confidence [Ex. F]. Nothing further.

ruling.holding: The Court finds a short practice position is warranted.

findings.finding: Spot price rose 0.82% in the last hour but remains near the lower third of its 24‑hour range
SOL is down 3.03% over seven days and sits 7.68% below its recent high
Fear & Greed Index fell from 55 to 48, indicating waning bullish sentiment
RSI is neutral (50.4) and realized volatility modest (2.35%/day), offering no bullish momentum

ruling.opinion: The exhibits show a modest intraday rise that is confined to the lower third of the daily range [Ex. A, B], while the seven‑day trend is clearly negative [Ex. C] and sentiment has slipped into neutral territory [Ex. F]. A neutral RSI and only modest volatility provide no upward catalyst [Ex. D]. Together these factors suggest downward pressure outweighs any short‑term upside, justifying a short practice position for the next 24 hours.
ruling.dissent: The Bull could argue that the price’s position above the lower bound of its range and the reliable Chainlink feed create a safe ceiling for a long trade, but the broader weekly decline and sentiment weakness outweigh that view.
